entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, the Net-Zero Industry Act (NZIA), re-authored against a
full-text capture of its Official Journal text (263,269 characters, Articles 1 through 49 plus recitals
and Annexes) that resolves the truncation this record was previously quarantined for (batch 008: the
item's only capture was cut off at 40,002 characters, mid-recital, before any operative Article).

FACT: "REGULATION (EU) 2024/1735 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 13 June 2024 on establishing a framework of measures for strengthening Europe’s net-zero technology manufacturing ecosystem" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, title citation. https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

FACT: "The general objective of this Regulation is to improve the functioning of the internal market by establishing a framework in order to ensure the Union’s access to a secure and sustainable supply of net-zero technologies, including by scaling up the manufacturing capacity of net-zero technologies and their supply chains to safeguard their resilience while contributing to achieving the Union’s climate targets and climate neutrality objective, as defined in Regulation (EU) 2021/1119, with a view to the decarbonisation of the Union’s economy and society, and by contributing to quality jobs in net-zero technologies, and thereby also improving the competitiveness of the Union." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 1(1), EUR-Lex/Cellar. https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union ." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 49(1). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

FACT: "It shall apply from 29 June 2024." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 49(2). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

*Analytical inference:* the regulation entered into force the day after its Official Journal publication
and applies from 29 June 2024, per its own Article 49; specific provisions (Section 8) carry their own
later application dates.

**Convention notes.** This brief applies the regulation's provisions to the workspace's operational
profile: a freight forwarder operating across air, road, and ocean modes on Americas, Europe, and Asia
trade lanes. The workspace is assessed in its freight-forwarder role, not as a manufacturer, project
promoter, contracting authority, or energy producer.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Specific components and specific machinery not covered in that annex may still fall under the scope of this Regulation where, on the basis of evidence provided to a national competent authority, the project promoter can prove, for example via market studies or off-take agreements, that the specific components or specific machinery are primarily used for the production of net-zero technologies" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, recital. https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific component or machinery a workspace client manufactures
or trades falls within this scope extension is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope; the
captured text extends the Regulation's scope on a case-by-case, evidence basis, not automatically.

*Operational implication:* the NZIA is a manufacturing-sector regulation. Its direct compliance
obligations fall on net-zero technology manufacturers, project promoters, Member State authorities,
contracting authorities, public bodies designing renewable-energy auctions, and authorised oil and gas
producers (Article 23). None of the captured operative text states an obligation running to a
freight-forwarding workspace.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Analytical inference:* because the NZIA's own compliance duties run to the entities named above and not
to freight forwarders, there is no immediate compliance action item for the workspace under this
regulation. The monitoring items below follow from the regulation's own dated provisions.

FACT: "Articles 26 and 28 shall apply from 30 December 2025." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 49(4). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

*Operational implication:* the auction resilience and sustainability criteria (Section 8) become binding
from 30 December 2025, per the regulation's own transitional provision; this is the nearest dated
milestone likely to affect the origin-documentation pressure on Asia-Europe technology and energy-
equipment cargo the workspace may see through its clients.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "Applications for recognition of net-zero technology manufacturing projects as net-zero strategic projects shall be submitted by the project promoter to the relevant Member State." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 14(1). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

FACT: "By 30 December 2024 Member States shall establish or designate one or more authorities as single points of contact at the relevant administrative level." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 6(1). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

FACT: "Each entity holding an authorisation as defined in Article 1, point 3, of Directive 94/22/EC shall be subject to an individual contribution to the Union-wide target for available CO 2 injection capacity set in Article 20 of this Regulation." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 23(1). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

FACT: "By 30 September 2024, Member States shall identify and report to the Commission the entities referred to in paragraph 1 and their volumes in crude oil and natural gas production from 1 January 2020 to 31 December 2023." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 23(2). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the captured text's compliance chain runs from project promoters
(applications, Article 14) and Member States (single points of contact, Article 6; permit-granting) to
contracting authorities and auction-designing public bodies (Section 8), and separately to authorised oil
and gas producers (Article 23). No obligation running from this Regulation to a freight-forwarding
workspace, carrier, or logistics intermediary is stated anywhere in the captured operative text.

*Analytical inference:* the workspace's position in this chain is that of a downstream logistics provider
potentially serving a project promoter, a contracting authority, or an auction winner named in the
captured Articles, not a party to the compliance mechanism itself.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of the date of this brief. No implementing act, delegated regulation, or
formal Commission guidance document under Regulation (EU) 2024/1735 is present in the captured source
pool, beyond the implementing-act delegations the regulation's own Articles name (Section 6).*

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "By 31 December 2027 and every two years thereafter, the Commission shall carry out a comprehensive assessment of the application of the resilience and sustainability criteria for auctions for the deployment of energy from renewable sources and their effect on the accelerated deployment of renewable energy technologies." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 26(8). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

*Operational implication:* the first biennial Commission assessment of the auction resilience and
sustainability criteria falls due 31 December 2027; a positive assessment can lead to a Commission proposal
to raise the volume shares in Article 26(7) (Section 8) toward the recital's own stated aspiration
(below), which the workspace should treat as the next material trigger for origin-documentation pressure
on relevant cargo.

FACT: "No later than 30 June 2026, Member States shall lay down penalties by means of administrative procedures, legal proceedings, or both, applicable to infringements by entities referred to in paragraph 1 with regard to their obligations under paragraph 3. Those penalties shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 23(13). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Member States must lay down penalties for oil and gas producers'
non-observance of their CO2-injection-capacity contribution obligations by 30 June 2026; this deadline and
penalty regime runs to Member States and authorised producers, not to the workspace.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does the workspace have any obligation to register, report, or notify under the NZIA?**

*Analytical inference:* No. The captured text's application, permitting, procurement, and auction
provisions (Articles 6, 9, 14, 15, 16, 25, 26) address project promoters, Member State authorities,
contracting authorities, and auction-designing public bodies; none names a freight-forwarding workspace as
an addressee.

**Q2: Does the auction resilience trigger create any documentation obligation for the workspace as
forwarder?**

FACT: "Auctions shall contribute to resilience, taking into account the proportion of the net-zero technology or its main specific components that originates from a third country accounting for more than 50 % of the supply of that specific net-zero technology or its main specific components within the Union." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 26(2). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this resilience mechanism runs to Member States designing renewable-energy
auctions, not to freight forwarders. If the workspace is asked by a client to provide origin certificates
or supply-chain documentation to support the client's own compliance with this criterion, the question of
accuracy, liability, and professional duty in providing such documentation requires legal review under
applicable EU customs and trade law.

**Q3: Does the procurement resilience trigger and its charge create any obligation for the workspace?**

FACT: "the proportion of a specific net-zero technology or its main specific components originating in a third country accounts for more than 50 % of the supply of that specific net-zero technology or its main specific components within the Union" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 25. https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

FACT: "an obligation to pay a proportionate charge, in the event of non-observance of the conditions referred in point (a) or (b), of at least 10 % of the value of the specific net-zero technologies of the contract referred to in this paragraph." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 25(7)(d). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

*Legal Confirmation Required:* both the resilience-trigger determination and the non-observance charge run
to the main contractor on a covered public procurement contract, not to a freight forwarder engaged
downstream of that contractor; whether the workspace's own logistics services to such a contractor create
any indirect exposure is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*As established above, the workspace bears no direct substantive compliance obligations under Regulation
(EU) 2024/1735. This section documents the regulation's substantive provisions as captured, with the
required slots stated first.*

**Required slots.**

FACT: "The general objective of this Regulation is to improve the functioning of the internal market by establishing a framework in order to ensure the Union’s access to a secure and sustainable supply of net-zero technologies, including by scaling up the manufacturing capacity of net-zero technologies and their supply chains to safeguard their resilience while contributing to achieving the Union’s climate targets and climate neutrality objective, as defined in Regulation (EU) 2021/1119, with a view to the decarbonisation of the Union’s economy and society, and by contributing to quality jobs in net-zero technologies, and thereby also improving the competitiveness of the Union." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 1(1). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

FACT: "The permit-granting process for net-zero strategic projects shall not exceed: (a) 9 months for the construction or expansion of net-zero strategic projects with a yearly manufacturing capacity of less than 1 GW; (b) 12 months for the construction or expansion of net-zero strategic projects with a yearly manufacturing capacity of 1 GW or more; (c) 18 months for all necessary permits to operate a storage site in accordance with Directive 2009/31/EC." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 16(1). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

FACT: "No later than 30 June 2026, Member States shall lay down penalties by means of administrative procedures, legal proceedings, or both, applicable to infringements by entities referred to in paragraph 1 with regard to their obligations under paragraph 3. Those penalties shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 23(13). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

FACT: "It shall apply from 29 June 2024." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 49(2). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

FACT: "Articles 26 and 28 shall apply from 30 December 2025." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 49(4). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

**Permitting streamlining.** FACT: "The permit-granting process for net-zero technology manufacturing projects shall not exceed any of the following time limits: (a) 12 months for the construction or expansion of net-zero technology manufacturing projects with a yearly manufacturing capacity of less than 1 GW; (b) 18 months for the construction or expansion of net-zero technology manufacturing projects with a yearly manufacturing capacity of 1 GW or more." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 9(1). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

*Operational implication:* faster permitting for net-zero manufacturing projects (including SAF and
battery/electrolyser production) in EU Member States accelerates the rate at which domestic production
capacity comes online for these technologies; the effect on the workspace's own carrier surcharge
trajectory requires carrier-specific data to quantify.

**Strategic project priority status.** FACT: "Project promoters and all authorities concerned shall ensure that for net-zero strategic projects the relevant processes are treated in the most rapid way possible in accordance with Union and national law." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 15(1). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

FACT: "where a project is recognised as a net-zero strategic project, Member States shall grant that net-zero strategic project the status of the highest national significance possible, where such a status exists in national law" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 15(2). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

**Net-zero Acceleration Valleys.** FACT: "Member States may decide to designate net-zero Acceleration Valleys (the ‘Valleys’) as specific areas to accelerate net-zero industrial activities, in particular to accelerate the implementation of net-zero technology manufacturing projects, including net-zero strategic projects or clusters thereof, or to test innovative net-zero technologies." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 17(1). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

**Public procurement sustainability and resilience conditions.** FACT: "the proportion of a specific net-zero technology or its main specific components originating in a third country accounts for more than 50 % of the supply of that specific net-zero technology or its main specific components within the Union" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 25. https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

FACT: "an obligation to pay a proportionate charge, in the event of non-observance of the conditions referred in point (a) or (b), of at least 10 % of the value of the specific net-zero technologies of the contract referred to in this paragraph." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 25(7)(d). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

FACT: "the detailed conditions under which the Commission may grant an exemption or a derogation to entities under paragraph 7, 8 or 11." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 23(12). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

FACT: "Until 30 June 2026, Article 25(1) shall apply only to contracts concluded by central purchasing bodies as defined in Article 2(1), point (16), of Directive 2014/24/EU and Article 2(1), point (12), of Directive 2014/25/EU and for contracts of a value equal to or higher than EUR 25 million." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 49(3). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

FACT: "Specific components and specific machinery not covered in that annex may still fall under the scope of this Regulation where, on the basis of evidence provided to a national competent authority, the project promoter can prove, for example via market studies or off-take agreements, that the specific components or specific machinery are primarily used for the production of net-zero technologies" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, recital. https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the exemption/derogation clause above applies to oil and gas producers'
CO2-injection-capacity contribution (Article 23), a different mechanism from the procurement charge; both
are recorded here as the captured text's own qualification vocabulary, not as interchangeable.

**Auction sustainability and resilience criteria for renewable energy deployment.** FACT: "Auctions shall contribute to resilience, taking into account the proportion of the net-zero technology or its main specific components that originates from a third country accounting for more than 50 % of the supply of that specific net-zero technology or its main specific components within the Union." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 26(2). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

FACT: "Paragraphs 1 to 5 shall apply to at least 30 % of the volume auctioned per year per Member State or alternatively to at least 6 Gigawatt per year per Member State." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 26(7). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

FACT: "contributing to meeting the overall objectives of this Regulation and to reaching 50 % by the end of 2029." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, recital. https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

*Operational implication:* Article 26(7)'s binding default is at least 30 % of auctioned volume per year
per Member State (or 6 Gigawatt/year); the recital's own stated aspiration is a gradual increase toward
50 % by the end of 2029, reviewable under the Article 26(8) biennial assessment (Section 6). The 30 %
figure is the current binding requirement; the 50 %-by-2029 figure is the regulation's own stated
direction of travel, not (per the captured operative text) itself a binding 2029 target.

**Manufacturing benchmarks and CO2 injection capacity.** FACT: "a benchmark of at least 40 % of the Union’s annual deployment needs for the corresponding technologies necessary to achieve the Union’s 2030 climate and energy targets" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 5(1)(a). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

FACT: "an increased Union share for the corresponding technologies with a view to reaching 15 % of world production by 2040 on the basis of monitoring pursuant to Article 42" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 5(1)(b). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

FACT: "An annual injection capacity of at least 50 million tonnes of CO 2 shall be achieved by 2030 in storage sites, meaning geological storage sites permitted under Directive 2009/31/EC including depleted oil and gas fields and saline aquifers, located in the territory of the Union, its exclusive economic zones or on its continental shelf within the meaning of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea and which are not combined with Enhanced Hydrocarbon Recovery." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 20(1). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

No phase-in is stated in Article 5 beyond the two dated benchmarks above (2030 and 2040); no further
per-year schedule is captured.

No exceptions are stated in Article 25 beyond the GPA-covered-contract exclusion and the Article 23(12)
exemption/derogation power captured above, which are recorded as FACT claims rather than absences.

No scope limits are stated in Article 1 beyond the case-by-case scope extension captured in Section 2,
which is recorded as a FACT claim rather than an absence.

Obligations surveyed: 16; workspace-adjacent: 3; extracted as FACT: 16.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section: the workspace does not sell products under its own name that fall within
the NZIA's scope of net-zero technology final products or components.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "By 30 December 2024 Member States shall establish or designate one or more authorities as single points of contact at the relevant administrative level." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 6(1). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

*Analytical inference:* the regulation's registration and reporting structures (single points of contact,
Member State progress reporting, oil and gas producer contribution reporting under Article 23) run between
Member States, project promoters, and the Commission; no registration or reporting obligation running to a
freight-forwarding workspace is stated anywhere in the captured operative text.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Analytical inference:* the captured text does not call for the workspace to operate any reporting,
monitoring, or registration system. The permit-granting and single-point-of-contact mechanisms (Articles 6,
9, 16) are government-to-project-promoter channels with no private freight-forwarder analogue stated.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "the detailed conditions under which the Commission may grant an exemption or a derogation to entities under paragraph 7, 8 or 11." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, Article 23(12). https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735

*Operational implication:* the Commission's power to grant an exemption or derogation under Article 23 is
specific to authorised oil and gas producers' CO2-injection-capacity contributions; it is not a general
exemption mechanism available to a freight-forwarding workspace.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No authoritative published research directly linking NZIA implementation to freight-forwarder operational
costs or competitive positioning is present in the source pool provided.*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 13 June 2024: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735 adopted by the European Parliament and Council.
- The day following OJ publication: entry into force, per the regulation's own Article 49(1).
- 29 June 2024: the regulation applies from this date, per Article 49(2).
- 30 December 2024: deadline for Member States to establish or designate single points of contact
  (Article 6(1)).
- 30 September 2024: deadline for Member States to identify and report authorised oil and gas producers
  (Article 23(2)).
- 30 December 2025: Articles 26 (auctions) and 28 apply from this date (Article 49(4)).
- Until 30 June 2026: Article 25(1) applies only to central purchasing bodies and contracts of EUR 25
  million or more (Article 49(3)); the full procurement scope applies after this date.
- 30 June 2026: deadline for Member States to lay down penalties for oil and gas producer non-observance
  (Article 23(13)).
- 2030: manufacturing benchmark of at least 40 % of Union annual deployment needs (Article 5(1)(a)); CO2
  injection capacity of at least 50 million tonnes annually (Article 20(1)).
- 31 December 2027 (and every two years thereafter): first Commission biennial assessment of the auction
  resilience and sustainability criteria (Article 26(8)).
- End of 2029: the recital's own stated aspiration for the auctioned-volume non-price-criteria share to
  reach 50 %, subject to the Article 26(8) review.
- 2040: secondary benchmark, 15 % of world production in value (Article 5(1)(b)).

*Source for timeline entries: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735, EUR-Lex/Cellar (https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1735).*

metadata.what_is_it: The EU Net-Zero Industry Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1735), re-authored from its full Official Journal text (Articles 1 through 49): permitting timelines, strategic-project status, procurement and auction resilience conditions, manufacturing benchmarks, and Member State penalty duties.
metadata.why_matters: It sets 2030 and 2040 EU manufacturing benchmarks and binding auction/procurement resilience conditions with real penalty and charge mechanisms; the workspace carries no direct compliance obligation but its clients procuring or bidding on net-zero technology may.
key_data: at least 40 percent of Union annual deployment needs met by domestic manufacturing by 2030 (Article 5)
15 percent of world production in value by 2040 (Article 5)
at least 50 million tonnes annual CO2 injection capacity by 2030 (Article 20)
10 percent of contract value charge for procurement non-observance (Article 25(7)(d))
at least 30 percent of auctioned volume subject to resilience criteria from 30 December 2025 (Article 26)
metadata.cost_mechanism: A proportionate charge of at least 10 percent of the value of the specific net-zero technologies of a covered public-procurement contract, payable by the main contractor for non-observance of origin-diversification conditions (Article 25(7)(d)).

steps.label: Article 49: in force the day after OJ publication, applies from 29 June 2024
Article 25(1) full scope after 30 June 2026 (Article 49(3)); Member State penalties due 30 June 2026 (Article 23(13))
at least 40 percent deployment-needs benchmark and 50 Mt CO2 injection capacity (Articles 5, 20)
15 percent of world production in value (Article 5(1)(b))

requirement_trajectory.note: the regulation phases its own binding thresholds across five dated milestones (2024/2025/2026/2030/2040), captured from its own operative Articles

metadata.penalty_range: at least 10 percent of contract value (procurement non-observance, Article 25(7)(d)); Member State-determined penalties, required to be effective, proportionate and dissuasive, for oil and gas producer non-observance (Article 23(13))
metadata.enforcement_body: Member States (penalties for oil and gas producer non-observance, Article 23(13); permit-granting and single-point-of-contact administration); the European Commission (Article 29(2) origin determinations; biennial auction-criteria assessment, Article 26(8)).

claims.source_span: By 30 September 2024, Member States shall identify and report to the Commission the entities referred to in paragraph 1 and their volumes in crude oil and natural gas production from 1 January 2020 to 31 December 2023.

claims.claim_text: [section6] Auction criteria biennial review clause, verbatim: 'By 31 December 2027 and every two years thereafter, the Commission shall carry out a comprehensive assessment of the application of the resilience and sustainability criteria for auctions for the deployment of energy from renewable sources and their effect on the accelerated deployment of renewable energy technologies.'
claims.source_span: By 31 December 2027 and every two years thereafter, the Commission shall carry out a comprehensive assessment of the application of the resilience and sustainability criteria for auctions for the deployment of energy from renewable sources and their effect on the accelerated deployment of renewable energy technologies.

claims.claim_text: [section6] Oil and gas producer penalty deadline, verbatim: 'No later than 30 June 2026, Member States shall lay down penalties by means of administrative procedures, legal proceedings, or both, applicable to infringements by entities referred to in paragraph 1 with regard to their obligations under paragraph 3. Those penalties shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.'
claims.source_span: No later than 30 June 2026, Member States shall lay down penalties by means of administrative procedures, legal proceedings, or both, applicable to infringements by entities referred to in paragraph 1 with regard to their obligations under paragraph 3. Those penalties shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.

claims.claim_text: [section7] Auction resilience trigger, verbatim: 'Auctions shall contribute to resilience, taking into account the proportion of the net-zero technology or its main specific components that originates from a third country accounting for more than 50 % of the supply of that specific net-zero technology or its main specific components within the Union.'
claims.source_span: Auctions shall contribute to resilience, taking into account the proportion of the net-zero technology or its main specific components that originates from a third country accounting for more than 50 % of the supply of that specific net-zero technology or its main specific components within the Union.

claims.claim_text: [section7] Procurement resilience trigger, verbatim: 'the proportion of a specific net-zero technology or its main specific components originating in a third country accounts for more than 50 % of the supply of that specific net-zero technology or its main specific components within the Union'

claims.claim_text: [section7] Procurement non-observance charge, verbatim: 'an obligation to pay a proportionate charge, in the event of non-observance of the conditions referred in point (a) or (b), of at least 10 % of the value of the specific net-zero technologies of the contract referred to in this paragraph.'
claims.source_span: an obligation to pay a proportionate charge, in the event of non-observance of the conditions referred in point (a) or (b), of at least 10 % of the value of the specific net-zero technologies of the contract referred to in this paragraph.

claims.claim_text: [section8] General permitting timeline, verbatim: 'The permit-granting process for net-zero technology manufacturing projects shall not exceed any of the following time limits: (a) 12 months for the construction or expansion of net-zero technology manufacturing projects with a yearly manufacturing capacity of less than 1 GW; (b) 18 months for the construction or expansion of net-zero technology manufacturing projects with a yearly manufacturing capacity of 1 GW or more.'

claims.claim_text: [section8] Strategic project priority processing, verbatim: 'Project promoters and all authorities concerned shall ensure that for net-zero strategic projects the relevant processes are treated in the most rapid way possible in accordance with Union and national law.'

claims.claim_text: [section8] Strategic project highest-status grant, verbatim: 'where a project is recognised as a net-zero strategic project, Member States shall grant that net-zero strategic project the status of the highest national significance possible, where such a status exists in national law'

claims.claim_text: [section8] Valleys designation power, verbatim: 'Member States may decide to designate net-zero Acceleration Valleys (the ‘Valleys’) as specific areas to accelerate net-zero industrial activities, in particular to accelerate the implementation of net-zero technology manufacturing projects, including net-zero strategic projects or clusters thereof, or to test innovative net-zero technologies.'

claims.claim_text: [section8] Exemption/derogation power, verbatim: 'the detailed conditions under which the Commission may grant an exemption or a derogation to entities under paragraph 7, 8 or 11.'

claims.claim_text: [section8] Article 25(1) transitional threshold, verbatim: 'Until 30 June 2026, Article 25(1) shall apply only to contracts concluded by central purchasing bodies as defined in Article 2(1), point (16), of Directive 2014/24/EU and Article 2(1), point (12), of Directive 2014/25/EU and for contracts of a value equal to or higher than EUR 25 million.'

claims.claim_text: [section8] Scope extension to specific components, verbatim: 'Specific components and specific machinery not covered in that annex may still fall under the scope of this Regulation where, on the basis of evidence provided to a national competent authority, the project promoter can prove, for example via market studies or off-take agreements, that the specific components or specific machinery are primarily used for the production of net-zero technologies'

claims.claim_text: [section8] Auction volume-share default, verbatim: 'Paragraphs 1 to 5 shall apply to at least 30 % of the volume auctioned per year per Member State or alternatively to at least 6 Gigawatt per year per Member State.'

claims.claim_text: [section8] Auction 2029 aspiration, verbatim: 'contributing to meeting the overall objectives of this Regulation and to reaching 50 % by the end of 2029.'

claims.claim_text: [section8] 2030 manufacturing benchmark, verbatim: 'a benchmark of at least 40 % of the Union’s annual deployment needs for the corresponding technologies necessary to achieve the Union’s 2030 climate and energy targets'

claims.claim_text: [section8] 2040 secondary benchmark, verbatim: 'an increased Union share for the corresponding technologies with a view to reaching 15 % of world production by 2040 on the basis of monitoring pursuant to Article 42'

claims.claim_text: [section8] CO2 injection capacity target, verbatim: 'An annual injection capacity of at least 50 million tonnes of CO 2 shall be achieved by 2030 in storage sites, meaning geological storage sites permitted under Directive 2009/31/EC including depleted oil and gas fields and saline aquifers, located in the territory of the Union, its exclusive economic zones or on its continental shelf within the meaning of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea and which are not combined with Enhanced Hydrocarbon Recovery.'

claims.claim_text: [section10] Single point of contact establishment duty, verbatim: 'By 30 December 2024 Member States shall establish or designate one or more authorities as single points of contact at the relevant administrative level.'
